title: ATE Estimation with Saturated Categorical Adjustment under a Weighted Effect-Energy Restriction
banked_reason: The delivered note does not determine the sharp finite-sample frontier for every radius; the central weighted-energy window remains open, and the field score ceiling is 6.7 < 7.4.
gap_reasons: The proposal headlines a sharp, total minimax frontier for every radius, but the delivered kernel leaves its central residual window open; retain the useful exterior-region results but position this as a partial frontier rather than the promised full result.

Its claim that the accepted maximum-deviation bracket did not expose the small-radius parametric region is inaccurate: the accepted all-alphabet result already matches the d=n maximum-deviation class when sigma-squared is of order 1/n; distinguish that inherited specialization from the new sharper large-radius analysis.
Its proof uses ass:overlap to ensure both occupied-arm means exist and to conclude |tau_k|<=1, but ass:overlap is not in depends_on.
The supportwise membership proof invokes consistency and conditional exchangeability for every embedded law, but neither ass:consistency nor ass:conditional-exchangeability is declared in depends_on.
proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted a matched finite-sample ATE minimax rate for every weighted-effect-variance radius. It derived an all-radius lower bound and upper envelope, with matching rates for σ² ≤ 1/n and σ² ≥ L_n n^(-3/4), but the intermediate window remains open; at σ² = L_n²/n the bracket differs by a logarithmic factor. The full-range weighted-energy versus maximum-deviation comparison is reusable, subject to the attribution and dependency corrections listed above.
tldr: Saturated categorical adjustment creates empirically uncrossed cells, so the precision gain from treatment-effect homogeneity depends on its geometry. Taking the standard identified ATE functional from Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy as a prerequisite, this project studies finite-sample risk with \(d=n\), unknown masses and propensities, and the population restriction \(V_\tau(P)\le\sigma^2\), which permits large effects in rare cells. A propensity-retaining Bernoulli-thinning image of Zeng et al.'s binary, zero-control source experiment proves the full radius-dependent converse on an anchor-aligned subclass; three explicit total estimators attain it whenever \(\sigma^2\le n^{-1}\) or \(\sigma^2\ge L_n n^{-3/4}\). The only unresolved weighted-energy interval is \(n^{-1}<\sigma^2<L_n n^{-3/4}\), including the two-scale point \(\sigma^2=L_n^2/n\). On the maximum-deviation class, direct inclusion supplies \(R_\infty(n,\sigma)\asymp n^{-1}\) for \(\sigma^2\le n^{-1}\), while a propensity-preserving reduction and the common-attenuation estimator give \(R_\infty(n,\sigma)\asymp\sigma^2/L_n^2\) for \(\sigma^2\ge L_n^2n^{-3/4}\); its remaining window is \(n^{-1}<\sigma^2<L_n^2n^{-3/4}\). Throughout \(L_n^2n^{-3/4}\le\sigma^2\le1\), \(R_2/R_\infty\asymp\min\{L_n,\sigma^{-2}\}\): weighted energy costs a factor \(L_n\) up to the saturation elbow \(\sigma^2=L_n^{-1}\), then a factor \(\sigma^{-2}\). The 401(k) eligibility and net-financial-assets analysis with 8,196 saturated cells is the empirical consumer, conditional on population overlap, outcome envelopes, and a substantively defended effect-energy radius.
gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy supply the causal identification prerequisite and leave sharp dependence on a maximum-deviation radius open, while Kwon and Sun analyze an empirical target-weighted VCATE ball conditional on a fixed design. Neither gives a random-design population-mass-weighted effect-energy frontier with arbitrary unknown masses and propensities.
fill: The project verifies a supportwise rare-subpopulation lower benchmark; evaluates exact occupancy, unrestricted-polynomial, and common-attenuation maps through a deterministic finite kernel; certifies the clipped attenuation range and the separate light--heavy routing; proves the matched regions and the class-and-rate distinction from the maximum-deviation bracket; and resolves the remaining window through the exact two-scale stabilization-or-converse program.
